 BREAKING: Man arrested, accused of shooting cousin in arm during fight at Riverchase Galleria Magic City Classic tailgaters say higher gas prices are not keeping them away 
 Fans who drove hundreds of miles to Legion Field said they have noticed higher prices at the pump this year 
 Gas prices impact on tailgaters at the Magic City Classic By Tanaisa Shaw Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 10:43 PM CDT | Updated : 15 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BIRMINGHAM, Ala. ( WBRC ) - Tailgaters who drove hundreds of miles to Legion Field for the 85th Magic City Classic said they have seen a difference in gas prices this year, but the cost is not stopping them from attending.
 The Magic City Classic says it’s the largest HBCU football game in the country. A&M and ASU are scheduled to face off at 2:30 p.m. on Saturday.
 Road trips to classic
 People traveled from across the country to take part in the event.
 Wilbur Swanson of Maryland said he made the trip to Birmingham from Maryland, outside of Washington, D.C.
 “Twelve hour drive. Roughly 850 miles,” Swanson said.
 Tiffany Commings of Loganville, Georgia, said her drive was “about 253 miles.”
 Gas prices compared to last year
 On Friday, the national average for a gallon of regular gas was $4.20, according to AAA. A year ago, the average was $3.04, a difference of more than $1.
 Commings said prices were lower when she made the trip last year.
 “The prices then were less, significantly less. It was probably like 40 to 50 cents less,” Commings said.
 Shonquis Ryan of Greensboro, Alabama, said she filled up her tank on Friday.
 “I filled up today. That took like $39,” Ryan said.
 Swanson said his cost has increased.
 “Normally runs $200, but I’ve seen that jump to $250, $260,” Swanson said.
 Commings said the trip is worth the cost.
 “I am coming to see family, so it’s worth it, but I am like, oh my gosh, this is ridiculous,” Commings said.
 Attendees weigh cost against the event
 People tailgating on Friday said they knew gas would be more expensive. They said celebrating legacy was more important than the added expense.
 “It’s the unity and love of family that drives me down here,” Swanson said.
 The national average for a gallon of regular gas has dropped five cents over the past week, according to AAA.
